summary: A short notice from BBN asking anyone who uses a TIP, the terminal-handling machine on the ARPANET, and was not getting updates to the TIP User's Guide or TIP User's Group Notes to send in their name so they could join the mailing list.

plainLanguage.summary: A request that people who use a certain kind of network terminal send in their names so they get the updated instruction booklets.

subtitle: A request for TIP users to join the distribution list for guides and newsletters.

tldr.problem: Some users of the TIP (Terminal Interface Processor) were not receiving the TIP User's Guide or the TIP User's Group Notes.
tldr.mechanism: BBN invited any TIP user not on the mailing list to send their name and the TIP and host they normally used, so they could be added to the distribution.
tldr.outcome: BBN ensured that all active TIP users could stay informed of updates and best practices.

today: RFC 457 documents user support procedures for TIP systems. The TIP was eventually superseded by more sophisticated terminal servers and the transition to TCP/IP-based network access.

sections.title: TIP User's Group
sections.content: RFC 457 is a brief administrative notice from BBN addressing the TIP User's Group (TIPUG). The TIP (Terminal Interface Processor) was a special-purpose computer that allowed regular terminals to connect to the ARPANET without requiring a full host computer. BBN maintained documentation and notes for TIP users, including the TIP User's Guide and TIP User's Group Notes.
sections.plainLanguage: The TIP was a box that let regular computer terminals connect to the network. BBN published guides for people using it.

sections.title: Joining the Mailing List
sections.content: Not all TIP users were receiving the latest documentation. RFC 457 asks any TIP user who was not receiving updates to send BBN their name, along with the identifier of the TIP and the host computer they normally used. BBN would then add them to the distribution list for future updates and notices.
sections.plainLanguage: If you used a TIP and were not getting the guides, you could write to BBN and they would put you on the mailing list.

sections.title: User Support Infrastructure
sections.content: This notice reflects BBN's commitment to maintaining an active community of TIP users and ensuring they had access to current documentation. The TIP User's Group (TIPUG) and the distribution mechanism for guides and notes were important parts of the support infrastructure for remote terminal users on the ARPANET. Proper communication channels helped users maximize the value they got from their TIP equipment.
sections.plainLanguage: BBN wanted to make sure everyone using a TIP got the latest guides so they could use it effectively.
